title: The JavaScript event loop
summary: A browser JavaScript lesson: run synchronous code, drain microtasks, then run another task. Follow all five steps on this canvas.

steps.title: Meet the four components
steps.explanation: The stack runs JavaScript. Browser APIs handle timers and events. Promise callbacks wait as microtasks; timer callbacks wait as tasks.
steps.takeaway: The browser schedules callbacks; the call stack executes them.

nodes.label: Call stack
nodes.detail: Runs the current JavaScript function calls.

nodes.label: Browser APIs
nodes.detail: Timers and events are managed by the browser.

nodes.label: Task queues
nodes.detail: Timer callbacks and events wait for a turn.

steps.title: Synchronous code runs first
steps.explanation: JavaScript executes the current script in order. A function call adds a stack frame, and returning removes it. Scheduled callbacks cannot interrupt this synchronous work.
steps.takeaway: Finish the current synchronous work before running queued callbacks.

nodes.label: Start script
nodes.detail: The browser begins executing the script.

nodes.label: Call a function
nodes.detail: Push a frame; execute its body.

nodes.label: Return
nodes.detail: Pop the frame and continue the script.

steps.title: Schedule the asynchronous work
steps.explanation: setTimeout asks the browser to schedule a callback later. A .then callback on an already resolved Promise goes into the microtask queue. The script keeps running.
steps.takeaway: A zero-millisecond timeout means eligible later, never immediately.

nodes.label: setTimeout(callback, 0)
nodes.detail: Timer becomes eligible; its callback waits as a task.

nodes.label: Promise.resolve().then(...)
nodes.detail: The reaction waits as a microtask.

steps.title: Microtasks have priority
steps.explanation: After the current script finishes, the browser drains the microtask queue, including newly added microtasks. It can then run another task. Rendering may happen between turns; it is not guaranteed after each task.
steps.takeaway: In this example, the Promise callback runs before the timer callback.

nodes.label: Finish current script
nodes.detail: Synchronous work completes and the stack is empty.

nodes.label: Drain microtasks
nodes.detail: Run queued microtasks until the queue is empty.

nodes.label: Run another task
nodes.detail: An eligible timer callback can now get a turn.

steps.title: Predict the output: A D C B
steps.explanation: A and D are synchronous. C is a Promise microtask, so it runs after the script. B is a timer task, so it runs after the microtasks. Read the code and trace the four logs below.
steps.takeaway: Output: A, D, C, B. Scheduling order alone does not determine callback order.
